comments.text: This is totally normal for Louisiana. The land in the southern areas is mostly swamps that were artificially built up for human habitation, but that doesn't mean it isn't all still swamp lands. This is going to get worse over time because as the population grows, the people change the natural landscapes, reroute the water drainage, and totally disturb natures natural paths. Throw in erosion from the constant rains and flooding that pecks away at the ground pushing the soil into the Gulf, and it's a weird rotational cycle of damage to property. This is why southern Louisiana was once one of the cheapest places to live. Every big hurricane that hits brings this scene.
